title: Prostatic Penetration of Linezolid (DiProLine)
official: Study of the Prostatic Penetration of Linezolid in Patients Who Underwent Endoscopic Enucleation of the Prostate.
summary: Linezolid is an antibiotic active against many Gram-positive bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains such as methicillin-resistant S. aureus and glycopeptide-resistant enterococci. It has excellent oral bioavailability, good tissue penetration (though this has not yet been studied in the prostate), and a satisfactory safety profile over short treatment periods. Febrile male urinary tract infections (UTIs) are common, potentially serious, and require an antibiotic that penetrates the prostate well. Enterococci account for 5 to 11% of the pathogens responsible for urinary tract infections. The treatment of enterococcal UTIs remains poorly defined, as the standard options for UTIs (fluoroquinolones, cotrimoxazole) have limitations in terms of efficacy. Given its pharmacological properties, linezolid could be a promising alternative for enterococcal UTIs, although no data to date confirm its penetration in the prostate.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Men aged 65 and older
* Confirmed diagnosis of benign prostatic hyperplasia (estimated prostate volume ≥ 60 mL) requiring a Endoscopic enucleation of the prostate performed at the Centre Hospitalier du Mans.
* Signed informed consent form.
* Patient enrolled in or covered by a social security program.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contraindications to the use of linezolid:

  * Known intolerance or allergy to linezolid.
  * Relative contraindications according to the Vidal database: acute confusional state, uncontrolled hypertension, hyperthyroidism, pheochromocytoma, dysthymic schizophrenia, carcinoid syndrome, bipolar disorder.
  * Medications not recommended or contraindicated for use with linezolid, according to the Vidal Interaction Database: monoamine oxidase-B inhibitors, bupropion, pethidine, piritramide, triptans, dextromethorphan, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, combined adrenergic-serotonergic medications, direct or indirect sympathomimetics, tramadol.
* Prostate cancer.
* Prostate biopsies performed during the same surgical procedure.
* Patient has a urinary catheter in place prior to Endoscopic enucleation of the prostate.
* Medical history that may affect a drug's bioavailability, such as bariatric surgery, malabsorption syndrome, or gastroparesis.
* Liver failure.
* Severe or end-stage chronic kidney disease (glomerular filtration rate \< 30 mL/min/1.73 m² according to CKD-EPI).
* History of epilepsy
* Individuals subject to legal guardianship
* Individuals unable to give informed consent
* Subjects currently participating in another interventional research protocol
